requirement_text: < 1,000 KV writes per day at 199 accounts; ≤ 1 write per alias change
record_type: instrumented simulation plus manual dashboard cross-check

simulation.instrumentation: test-only IKvWriter that counts every PutAsync and DeleteAsync (including deletes of absent keys), stamped with the timestamp of an injected advancing TimeProvider
services_driven: AdminKvSyncService.SyncAsync (fullSync:true for the initial projection, fullSync:false at the end of the day)
simulation.interpretation: 226 writes/day in steady state; 427/day when the one-off empty-namespace projection is folded into the same 24 h window. Both are below 1,000. Every mutating KV call is counted, so the figure is conservative relative to state changes.

dashboard_cross_check.source: Cloudflare dashboard (authoritative billing view), not GraphQL analytics
dashboard_cross_check.window_label: November billing month to date, read 18 Nov 2026

mutating_operations.note: QR3.2 compares writes + deletes = 63; Cloudflare bills reads, writes, deletes and lists as separate operation classes, so the full billed-operation count is 240.

verdict: PASS - 226 writes in 24 h (427 including the initial projection) is below 1,000, one write per alias change, and the first dashboard billed-count cross-check is recorded for the November month-to-date window.
reproduction: Open the dashboard URL above while signed in and read the operation counts for the postern-kv namespace.
caveats: The simulation is a deterministic unit-test harness over the real application services with an in-memory IKvWriter; it is not a production traffic replay. It counts API-side writes only and does not include the Worker mail path, which performs 0 KV writes (see QR2.4 / worker/test/kv-budget.test.ts).
Every PutAsync and DeleteAsync call counts, including deletes of absent keys. Cloudflare bills the API operation, so this is conservative versus counting only state changes.

The initial empty-namespace full sync (201 writes) is reported separately and also folded into the 24 h total (427) for a stricter comparison, even though in practice it is a one-off bootstrap rather than a recurring daily cost.

Dashboard figures are the current billing month to date as read on 18 Nov 2026, not a completed 30-day invoice; the 63 mutating operations are far below the simulated daily budget but are not themselves a 24 h measurement. GraphQL analytics was not used as the billing source.

Cloudflare charges each operation class separately (reads, writes, deletes, lists); the 1,000/day QR3.2 budget is a write-count budget, so the comparison uses writes + deletes = 63 and reports the 240 all-class total for context.
